correctness.rationale: Greedy arch count equals subsequence-universality index by constructive matching and the completion-letter absent-subsequence witness. Exactly k occurrences of b force unique factorization into k arches ba or a^(u+1)b and terminal a^v, with sum of extras r. Pair counts split into T=binom(k,2) cross-arch pairs and sum_i epsilon_i(1+(k-i+1)u_i). Formal geometric products give the exact all-k>=4,r expression; reversal proves reciprocal symmetry and coefficient extraction proves all edge formulas. An independently defined brute subsequence test agreed for 6,441 words across 25 pairs, and did not substitute for the general proof.

value.rationale: Exact all-k>=4,r,C conditioned distributions answer a natural density/counting question inside binary Parikh-matrix classes recently investigated for exists/forall universality. A complete uniform coefficient product and edge stratification exploit the mathematically meaningful saturation boundary min(|w|a,|w|b)=k. The result determines finer information not recoverable merely from the aggregate count at fixed word length, without claiming a full unsaturated census.
